LA-2026-HB1.s: Provides funding for the normal operating costs of Louisiana state government for fiscal year 2026-2027. It covers many state departments and offices. It became Act No. 3 and took effect on 07/01/2026, with some line-item vetoes.

LA-2026-HB1017.s: Louisiana would change how courts divide community property after a divorce for full-time firefighters. Any pay increase earned after the marriage ends, if it depends on passing a written exam and a work test, would not be counted in a former spouse’s share of that property. The law became Act No. 968 and took effect on June 25, 2026.

LA-2026-HB1028.s: The law requires the Louisiana Department of Health to set Medicaid pay rates for nonemergency medical transportation, including wheelchair-accessible rides, at no less than $14.50 per trip and $2.10 per mile. It also requires a rate method for trips with more than one passenger and says rides to Medicaid care outside a person's parish or nearby parishes need a medical need finding. The law took effect on 06/25/2026 and was projected to increase state costs by $2,601,174.

LA-2026-HB1038.s: The law changes how a marshal can appoint deputy marshals. It lets the marshal issue commissions to deputy marshals, but only with approval from the local governing authority, which must also insure approved deputies. Local governing bodies must tell the marshal each year how many commissions can be issued, and if a marshal’s area crosses into a ward, the larger local government makes that choice. It became Act No. 866 and takes effect on 01/01/2027.

LA-2026-HB1062.s: The law changes how the Special School District board is chosen and run. It removes the rule that each governor-appointed member must come from a different public health region, and it requires nominee lists to be sent to the governor by August 1 each year. It also shifts textbook selection to the superintendent, requires yearly reviews of the superintendent, and repeals several board powers over land, property, and some school materials. The act takes effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB1082.s: The law changes where lawsuits about the Municipal Police Employees' Retirement System must be filed. Instead of East Baton Rouge Parish or the system's home parish, actions involving the system or its board of trustees must be brought in the district court for the parish where the employer is located. It became Act No. 936 and takes effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB1084.s: Public colleges and universities in Louisiana would be allowed to set and change some tuition and mandatory fee amounts themselves instead of leaving that to their management boards. The bill also lets them charge different tuition for some graduate, professional, special, and high-cost undergraduate programs, and it keeps student notice and hardship waiver rules in place. Tuition and fee increases could not be more than 10% over one year, and each school would have to file a yearly report on how it is using these charges.

LA-2026-HB1095.s: The law sets up a rebate for certain nursing facilities that install solar power systems as an alternative power source. To qualify, a facility must meet state emergency power rules and submit proof of its costs and installation. The rebate program starts January 1, 2027, ends January 1, 2029, and total rebates are capped at $2 million; the act became effective August 1, 2026.

LA-2026-HB1117.s: The law changes how some insurance payments affect the time limit for filing a claim. It says an insurer’s payment under certain policy terms does not count as an admission of debt or extend that time limit, and it requires written notice of that for some homeowners’ claims. The new rule on some parts takes effect January 1, 2027; the rest took effect when the governor signed it.

LA-2026-HB1126.s: This act sets money for the Louisiana Legislature for fiscal year 2026-2027. It covers pay and expenses for the House, Senate, legislative staff, the legislative auditor, the Legislative Fiscal Office, and the Louisiana State Law Institute. It became law and takes effect on 07/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB1153.s: Creates a rule that lets parish and city leaders declare temporary bans on outdoor burning when fire risk is high. It covers open burning such as yard debris, land clearing, construction debris, and some outdoor fires, with exceptions for farm burns, certified prescribed burns, and cooking fires in grills or smokers. People who break a ban can face local fines, may have to pay fire response costs, and can face higher criminal penalties if the fire causes major property damage or harms critical infrastructure. The act became law and takes effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB1161.s: This act lets the state transportation department transfer certain state property in Lafourche Parish to the city of Thibodaux. The deal excludes mineral rights, which stay with the state, and must be for an amount tied to the property’s appraised value. It became law on June 9, 2026, as Act No. 880.

LA-2026-HB1186.s: This law updates parts of Louisiana’s Uniform Construction Code and rules for inspector licensing. It makes small wording and section reference changes in the state code. It became Act No. 881 on June 9, 2026.

LA-2026-HB1189.s: Starting August 1, 2026, freshwater charter boat fishing guides in Louisiana must have a U.S. Coast Guard captain's license, along with the state guide license, proof of insurance, and the right state fishing license. The bill also removes a rule that required the Department of Wildlife and Fisheries to send written notice about other legal requirements. It became Act No. 937.

LA-2026-HB119.s: This law changes Louisiana rules on deepfakes and AI-made images of other people. It adds a new crime for possessing such images and raises penalties for sharing or selling them, with tougher penalties when a minor is shown or when the offender is an educator and the person shown is a student. It also tells schools to share information with students and parents about these consequences, and it took effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB1194.s: The bill would expand Louisiana’s Healthy Food Retail Act to cover food deserts, which are low-income areas far from a supermarket. It would let the Agriculture and Forestry Department fund more fresh food projects with grants and loans, including markets, mobile food projects, and related food access work. It would also require the department to map food deserts, write a 10-year plan, and send yearly reports to lawmakers. The governor vetoed the bill.

LA-2026-HB1199.s: Louisiana Act No. 884 requires many health plans to cover genetic testing for SCN2A-related conditions when ordered by a treating doctor or advanced practice provider. It also requires coverage for medically needed treatment, such as seizure medicine, therapy, equipment, and feeding or digestive care. The law lets plans use prior approval and cost sharing, but not more than they use for other covered care, and it does not apply to limited benefit plans.

LA-2026-HB1223.s: The law creates a statewide system to speed up early clinical trials in Louisiana and improve patient access to study treatments. It requires hospitals, health care providers, schools, and other research groups that run covered clinical trials in the state to join the system and sign a participation agreement. The state economic development agency must set up checklists, contact points, and response time goals, and it may help coordinate with sponsors, research groups, and patients.

LA-2026-HB1228.s: This act updates rules for hearing aid dealers in Louisiana. It changes what must be on a sale contract, adds an email address, and adjusts the rules for a 30-day return period and a 3-business-day cancel period for hearing aid purchases. It also changes some license rules, exam rules, and notice rules for dealer business locations. The law takes effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB1236.s: The law changes how pharmacy benefit managers pay pharmacies and pharmacists for prescription drugs. It requires them to include a professional dispensing fee in their payment formula and says they cannot take that fee back from a pharmacy, pharmacist, or member. It also lets the insurance commissioner ask for claim data to check compliance. It took effect on June 12, 2026.

LA-2026-HB1243.s: This act changes how the Sewerage and Water Board of New Orleans is set up and how some of its members are chosen. It adds a selection committee, sets term limits and residency rules for citizen members, lets the mayor send a stand-in to board meetings, and allows the board to reduce or forgive some water and sewer debts in set cases. It also sets quarterly planning meetings with state and parish officials on flood and drainage issues. The law takes effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB1249.s: The law sets rules for school-based health center services for students in Louisiana public schools. If a parent or adult student agrees, school staff could not block needed care, and public school boards with these services would have to adopt a public policy for how they work. It also says the state school board must write rules, and it takes effect on August 1, 2026.

LA-2026-HB1252.s: The law expands the city court areas in Marksville and Bunkie in Avoyelles Parish and sets who votes for the city judge and marshal in each area. It also gives both courts small claims power and shared power with the 12th Judicial District Court over some misdemeanor, civil, and juvenile cases, with a $50,000 limit for civil cases. It raises some court fines and says the new court area rules apply only to cases filed on or after January 1, 2027. It became law on June 25, 2026.

LA-2026-HB1256.s: This law sets rules for abandoned digital assets like cryptocurrency, virtual currency, and digital wallets. It says when these assets count as abandoned, how holders must report and turn them over, and when they may be sold or changed into cash. It also sets notice rules for owners and takes effect on 01/01/2027.

LA-2026-HB153.s: This law stops criminal court fines and fees from being sent to the state debt recovery office for collection. It also bars those debts from being reported to a credit bureau or other consumer reporting agency. It took effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB159.s: Creates a pilot program in Caddo Parish that would let the sheriff use active electronic monitoring as an alternative to jail for some eligible defendants before trial. It would require written rules, risk checks, monthly mental health checks for some people, and approval from the court, sheriff, and district attorney before someone joins. The law also sets rules for electronic monitoring providers, funding, reporting, and limits when the sheriff or parish can be held responsible for harm caused by a participant, and it became law on June 9, 2026.

LA-2026-HB166.s: The law removes Vermilion Parish from the Acadiana Regional Juvenile Justice District. It also cuts the district board from 11 members to 10 and removes one commissioner seat tied to Vermilion Parish. It became law on June 22, 2026.

LA-2026-HB2.s: Provides the state capital outlay budget for Louisiana for fiscal year 2026-2027, covering projects and improvements for state government, state schools, and other public entities. It sets rules for how project funding, bond sales, and priority changes would work, including different funding levels for projects in priorities 1 through 5. The measure became Act No. 4 and takes effect July 1, 2026, with one or more line-item vetoes.

LA-2026-HB211.s: Creates a Homelessness Court program in district courts to give eligible people experiencing homelessness a treatment-based court process. It lets a judge place qualifying defendants on supervised treatment and probation for at least 12 months, with counseling, job and housing help, and court-ordered drug or alcohol testing. It also creates a new crime for unauthorized camping on public property and bars public camping and temporary outdoor living, with some exceptions and notice rules. The law took effect when it was signed and became Act No. 788.

LA-2026-HB227.s: Court filings in Louisiana would be allowed on letter-size paper instead of only legal-size paper. The change would apply to filings in civil and criminal cases made by lawyers, whether on paper or sent electronically. It became Act No. 927 and takes effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB258.s: The bill would add several exceptions to Louisiana’s dual officeholding rules. It would let volunteer firefighters, some unpaid advisory group members, certain judicial branch workers, some school and college education staff, and qualified federal court reporters serve in listed public roles at the same time. It also says a judge ad hoc paid by the day is not a public employee for Ethics Board service. It became law on June 9, 2026.

LA-2026-HB312.s: The bill provides extra state money for fiscal year 2025-2026, mainly for state retirement systems. It sends funds to the Louisiana School Employees' Retirement System, the State Police Retirement System, the State Employees' Retirement System, and the Teachers' Retirement System to help pay old retirement debt. It became Act No. 961 and took effect on June 18, 2026.

LA-2026-HB316.s: The bill would require teacher prep programs for early grades, special education, and secondary teachers to include training on how to teach reading and literacy, including how to use reading screeners and student data. It would also require the state education department to create an adolescent literacy program, approve reading tests, and offer literacy training and coaching support for schools. Public schools would have to review student reading and related support plans each year in the first eight weeks of school. The act takes effect on August 1, 2026.

LA-2026-HB352.s: Changes the rules for behavioral health services for public school students. It requires school governing authorities to post their policy online and in student handbooks, and it allows these services during school hours, even in the classroom, when the student’s parent or guardian provides the needed evaluation and treatment plan. It also sets definitions for terms like evaluator and medically necessary services, and it takes effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB383.s: This act sets state money for the 2026-2027 year to run several agency ancillary funds, also called internal service funds, auxiliary accounts, or enterprise funds. It affects state offices and agencies such as Group Benefits, Risk Management, Property Assistance, Prison Enterprises, Technology Services, the Division of Administrative Law, and State Procurement, and it also sets rules for how those funds are handled. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.

LA-2026-HB401.s: This act names the elevated part of U.S. Highway 190 over the Bogue Falaya River in Covington, St. Tammany Parish, as the Corporal Justin D. McLeese Memorial Bridge. It also directs the state transportation department or its contractors to put up and keep signs for the name if local or private money covers the cost, up to $2,250 per sign. The law takes effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB410.s: The law requires a person to tell all people in a direct in-person conversation before using a device to record or transcribe it. It applies to private conversations, with exceptions for public or semi-public meetings, law enforcement work, emergencies, some public duties, and recording police in places a person may lawfully be. A person who breaks the rule can be ordered to pay damages, court costs, and reasonable lawyer fees. It became law and takes effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB414.s: This law changes rules for criminal background checks and hiring for certain health care workers and people who work in therapeutic group homes. It expands who is covered, lets hospitals use certain consumer reporting agencies for checks, allows temporary or conditional work in some cases while a check is still pending, and sets a single list of crimes that can block hiring. It also updates who at therapeutic group homes must get a background check.

LA-2026-HB463.s: Louisiana law raises the most a communications district can charge for wireless emergency phone service from $1.25 to $2 a month for each wireless connection. It affects wireless phone users in districts that levy this charge. The change takes effect on January 1, 2027.

LA-2026-HB468.s: Louisiana law now sets rules for wholesaling residential real estate. It requires written disclosures and a cancellation notice for sellers, and it says who gets any deposit if the deal is ended. It also bars certain acts by wholesalers, and violations can lead to a civil penalty of up to $5,000 per violation. The law takes effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB481.s: This law requires parish and city governments and school boards to use a contract to publish official proceedings and public notices. It also raises the highest allowed publishing rates to 3 cents per character in all parishes, with higher rates for tabular or prebuilt notices figured by square inch. It took effect on August 1, 2026.

LA-2026-HB593.s: The law raises the most a local government can charge for each service or transaction at some motor vehicle field offices that are not fully funded by the state, from $4.50 to $8. The money must still be used for office costs like rent, utilities, and upkeep. It also removes the special fee limits for Orleans, Jefferson, Calcasieu, and West Monroe. It became Act No. 948 and takes effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB688.s: Would add Atlantic tarpon to the list of saltwater game fish in Louisiana law and update the names of some other saltwater game fish. It would affect people and rules tied to that fish definition, and the bill was later vetoed by the governor.

LA-2026-HB707.s: The law lets the Liquefied Petroleum Gas Commission make agreements with the Department of Agriculture and Forestry to help promote liquefied petroleum gas. It changes who can serve on the advisory board, including allowing people with industry work experience, and sets rules for board meetings, quorum, and proxy voting. It took effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB708.s: Becomes law in East Baton Rouge Parish and gives justice of the peace courts the same power as city courts over eviction cases for leased homes, businesses, and farmland when the monthly rent is $5,000 or less. It also says the court's area matches its district lines.

LA-2026-HB723.s: The act lets riders of certain two-wheeled vehicles, plus mopeds, trimobiles, bicycles, and electric bicycles, go through a red light at some intersections with vehicle sensors after waiting two signal cycles or two minutes, whichever comes first. They must treat the light like a stop sign, decide it is safe, and yield to people in the crosswalk and to other vehicles. It became Act No. 951 and takes effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB732.s: The act gives the Louisiana Office of Motor Vehicles commissioner, or a designee, the power to temporarily pause certain fees, penalties, or license suspensions for up to 30 days when a person needs access to life-saving medicine or medical treatment and has proof from a health care provider. It also suspends the hybrid vehicle road usage fee for non-plugin hybrids until August 1, 2027, and says unpaid amounts for that fee cannot be treated as collectable debt. The act took effect on June 25, 2026.

LA-2026-HB75.s: This act creates a one-year pilot program for certain slot machine operators to offer more promotional play wagers, raising the untaxable amount from $5 million to $7 million. It also sets rules for how those proceeds are handled and says local governments and other local funds must not get less than they received in the 2025-2026 fiscal year. Licensees must file a report by March 1, 2027, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026, then ends June 30, 2027.

LA-2026-HB762.s: This law stops the Office of Motor Vehicles from sending certain unpaid reinstatement fee debts to the Office of Debt Recovery. It affects people who owe those fees because of no insurance or a lapse in coverage. It took effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB782.s: This law changes Louisiana rules for vapor products, alternative nicotine products, and modified risk tobacco products. It creates a three-step permit system for vapor products, raises some permit fees, bars certain manufacturers, wholesalers, and retailers from holding mixed permits or buying and selling in some direct ways, and bans selling products with a nicotine analogue. It also lowers the tax on certain modified risk tobacco products, changes stamp discounts, and took effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB812.s: Parish assessors would get a 5% annual increase in pay each year through 2029. The increase would apply only if the assessor gives public notice in the parish’s official journal twice, with the last notice at least 30 days before the raise. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.

LA-2026-HB848.s: This law changes rules for all-terrain vehicle dealers and now includes golf carts in those rules. It says dealers must have repair and service facilities for these vehicles, or use a nearby third-party service provider, a manufacturer-backed service option, or a manufacturer-authorized service provider. Before a sale, dealers must give buyers written details about where warranty repairs will happen and may need to note if some service is done at a remote site.

LA-2026-HB870.s: The law changes how health plans place some generic drugs and biosimilars on their drug lists, called formularies. It requires certain plans to add a lower-cost generic or biosimilar with better cost-sharing when the drug meets the bill’s cost rules, and it limits extra hurdles like prior approval or step therapy for those drugs. It also lets insurers use a net cost calculation for formulary placement and requires notice to the insurance commissioner, with some plan data kept confidential. The law takes effect August 1, 2026.

LA-2026-HB933.s: Creates a commemorative birth certificate that people can request for a $50 fee. It would be made for display, may show the state seal and the governor’s signature, and would count as evidence like a certified birth certificate copy. The law takes effect on 08/01/2026 and became Act No. 1.

LA-2026-HB944.s: Creates the Louisiana Women's Health Consortium within the state health department to study and guide women's health issues. The group would include public and private members, meet regularly, and write yearly reports on its work. It would also make a state health agenda, track funding needs, and help share trusted health information.

LA-2026-HB949.s: The law changes rules for the Louisiana State Radiologic Technology Board of Examiners and the people it licenses or permits. It says a "limited purpose permit" is not the same as a temporary working permit, and it updates several references to use "temporary working permit". It also changes one fee phrase to just "fees". It takes effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB953.s: The law moves plumbing license rules to the State Licensing Board for Contractors and ends the State Plumbing Board. It also sets new license types for apprentice, journeyman, and master plumbers, and keeps current plumbing licenses in place. It takes effect as stated in the act and became law on June 12, 2026.

LA-2026-HB956.s: The law changes rules on fireworks and fire safety. It says some requirements must follow National Fire Protection Association rules, and it updates a reference to the American Pyrotechnics Association. It also expands who may have to pay for certain operator and blaster credentials, and it took effect on 08/01/2026.

LA-2026-HB983.s: The law sets aside $229,647,995 for the Louisiana judiciary for fiscal year 2026-2027. It covers the Supreme Court, courts of appeal, district courts, the Criminal District Court of Orleans Parish, and other courts, along with related court programs and expenses. It took effect on July 1, 2026.

LA-2026-SB131.s: The law limits when professional and occupational boards can start discipline cases and when they must give written notice and hold a hearing. It sets time limits that vary by the type of complaint, such as negligence, fraud, or a rules violation, and it pauses those deadlines while a related legal case is pending. The hearing deadline does not apply to the Louisiana Professional Engineering and Land Surveying Board or the State Board of Architectural Examiners, and the law takes effect on 8/1/2026.

LA-2026-SB163.s: The law repeals the sunset date for Louisiana’s rules on virtual currency businesses. That means the current licensing and regulation system for these businesses would keep going past July 1, 2027. It takes effect on August 1, 2026.

LA-2026-SB25.s: This act changes the pay schedule for parish registrars of voters, chief deputy registrars, and confidential assistants. It raises the salary steps and changes how parish population is used to set pay. It took effect on June 22, 2026, and the fiscal note says it increases state general fund spending by $496,168.

LA-2026-SB387.s: This act changes rules for pharmacy benefit managers, which are companies that help manage prescription drug benefits for health plans. It sets duties and limits for these companies, adds data-sharing and cost rules, and lets the insurance commissioner charge fees and fines to help enforce the law. It also changes how the state buys pharmacy benefit manager services, including a reverse auction process.

LA-2026-SB401.s: Creates a Prescription Drug Affordability Board in Louisiana’s insurance department. The board would pick up to 10 drugs each year and require drug makers to report price increases and related cost data, while keeping that data private. It became law on June 12, 2026, as Act No. 915.

LA-2026-SB414.s: This act creates the Louisiana Medical Debt Protection Act. It caps interest on medical debt for medically necessary care at 2% a year, limits when wages or bank accounts can be garnished, and bars liens or foreclosure on a primary home or primary vehicle for that debt. It also lets the attorney general enforce the law and gives people a right to sue for harm; it took effect on June 9, 2026.

LA-2026-SB42.s: Louisiana would expand its child sexual abuse materials law to include images or other visuals of a child made by electronic or digital means, including artificial intelligence, if they look real to a reasonable person. It would also treat causing artificial intelligence to create these materials as producing them. The law takes effect August 1, 2026, and it became Act No. 892.

LA-2026-SB43.s: The law creates a state program in the Louisiana Department of Health for psychedelic-assisted therapy. It sets up ways to find study sites and patients, lets the state use opioid settlement money and other funds for this work, and requires reports to the department and legislature. It also lets academic health centers work with drug makers on clinical trials and sets rules for sharing any money from new intellectual property, including at least 2.5% of net sales royalties to the state. It takes effect August 1, 2026.

LA-2026-SB449.s: The law changes how some public contracts can be used to buy materials and goods. It lets a local government that owns or runs a railroad buy used or non-new locomotives, on-track equipment, other rolling stock, and track repair equipment, along with parts for them. It also explains that “non-new” means items that are used, rebuilt, reconditioned, reclaimed, or otherwise not new. It became Act No. 900 and takes effect on 8/1/2026.

LA-2026-SB485.s: The bill would give the city of St. George sole power to levy, collect, administer, and enforce an insurance premium tax on risks inside the city limits. It would stop Baton Rouge and East Baton Rouge Parish, including the consolidated government, from collecting that tax in St. George. The change would take effect on January 1, 2027, and apply only to premiums tied to periods starting on or after that date.

LA-2026-SB487.s: The bill would change the rules for leases used in charitable bingo, keno, and raffle games. It would require these lease terms to be agreed to in writing, and it keeps the rule that rent cannot be more than the fair market rate or be tied to game receipts or profits. It would take effect on August 1, 2026.
